description_summary: 12-month unduplicated enrollment headcounts broken down by student level, degree/certificate-seeking status, undergraduate attendance status, student entry status, sex, and race/ethnicity. Each record is uniquely identified by UNITID and EFFYALEV; undergraduate detail includes full-/part-time and degree/certificate-seeking versus nondegree/certificate-seeking students, with degree-seeking students further divided into first-time, transfer-in, and continuing categories. Beginning with 2019–20 data, nonbinary-gender counts are available only for total undergraduate and total graduate levels, not for the detailed undergraduate or attendance-status categories.

12-month unduplicated enrollment headcounts broken down by student level and distance-education status. Each record is uniquely identified by UNITID and EFFYDLEV and contains total enrollment, enrollment exclusively in distance education, enrollment in some distance education, and enrollment in no distance education.

12-month instructional activity measured by total credit hours and/or contact hours, reported separately for undergraduate and graduate activity. The table is organized by institution (UNITID) and instructional level, rather than by student demographic or distance-education characteristics, and supports deriving 12-month full-time-equivalent enrollment.

Institution-level academic library data for fiscal year 2022, covering library characteristics, physical and electronic collections, expenditures, services, and full-time-equivalent library staff. The survey applies only to degree-granting institutions; expenditure data are available only for institutions with total expenditures over $100,000. Information on physical and electronic serials is available from fiscal year 2017 onward.

Institution-level admissions records for the undergraduate selection process of entering first-time, degree/certificate-seeking students, including admission considerations, applicants, admitted applicants, admitted students who enrolled, and SAT/ACT scores. The table applies only to institutions without an open-admissions policy for entering first-time students; SAT/ACT measures are reported for institutions that require test scores for admission. For Fall 2022, the record grain is one institution, with additional gender categories for students outside the reported men/women categories, and 50th-percentile test scores available for the first time.

Awards and degrees conferred by six-digit 2020 CIP program, first or second major, award level, race/ethnicity, and gender. Each record is uniquely identified by UNITID, CIPCODE, MAJORNUM, and AWLEVEL; it contains total, men’s, and women’s awards, including race/ethnicity breakdowns. The less-than-one-year certificate category is split into less than 12 weeks and 12 weeks to less than one year.

Students receiving any award or degree, broken down by race/ethnicity and gender. There is one record per institution, uniquely identified by UNITID, with total, men’s, and women’s student counts and race/ethnicity breakdowns; this table does not distinguish programs or award levels.

Students receiving awards or degrees broken down by award level, race/ethnicity, gender, and age group. Each record is uniquely identified by UNITID and AWLEVEL; age counts cover under 18, 18–24, 25–39, and 40 or older, but race, gender, and age cannot be cross-tabulated together. Variables for students outside the IPEDS men/women categories are available for 2021–22, and less-than-one-year certificates are split into less than 12 weeks and 12 weeks to less than one year.

Programs offered and programs available entirely through distance education, broken down by six-digit 2020 CIP program and award level. Records are keyed by UNITID and CIPCODE and identify award levels offered, award levels for which all programs can be completed entirely by distance education, and award levels for which some can; two-digit CIP and CIP 99 records provide program-count summaries. Detailed distance-education categories and the split less-than-one-year certificate levels are available from 2019–20 onward.

Fall enrollment counts broken down by gender, full- or part-time attendance status, and student level. Each record is uniquely identified by IPEDS ID (UNITID), attendance status, and student level (EFLEVEL), with total and men’s and women’s counts, including full- and part-time totals.

Fall enrollment counts broken down by race/ethnicity, gender, full- or part-time attendance status, and student level. Records are uniquely identified by IPEDS ID (UNITID), attendance status, and student level (EFALEVEL); the table includes nine race/ethnicity categories. Beginning in fall 2022, nonbinary-gender information is available only for total undergraduate and total graduate levels, not for detailed undergraduate levels or attendance-status groups.

Fall enrollment counts broken down by distance-education status and student level. Records are uniquely identified by IPEDS ID (UNITID) and student level (EFDELEV); counts distinguish students exclusively in distance education, in some distance education, and in none, with exclusive-distance students further classified by location relative to the institution and the United States.

Fall enrollment counts broken down by age category, gender, full- or part-time attendance status, and student level. Records are uniquely identified by IPEDS ID (UNITID), age category (EFBAGE), and student level (LSTUDY). Enrollment by age is optional in even-numbered years, so 2022 (even) is an optional reporting year and data may be missing for institutions that did not report.

First-time freshman counts broken down by state of residence, including counts who graduated from high school in the previous year. Records are uniquely identified by IPEDS ID (UNITID) and state of residence (EFCSTATE). Enrollment by residence is optional in odd-numbered years, so 2022 (even) is not an optional year and the odd-year availability caveat does not remove data for this year.

Fall enrollment counts in selected major fields—Education, Engineering, Biological/Life Sciences, Mathematics, Physical Sciences, Business, Law, Dentistry, and Medicine—broken down by race/ethnicity, gender, attendance status, and student level. This table covers 4-year institutions only; records are uniquely identified by IPEDS ID (UNITID), major field, attendance status, and student level (EFCIPLEV). Fall enrollment by major is not collected in odd-numbered years, so 2022 (even) has data.

Institution-level measures of total entering class, first-year retention rate, and student-to-faculty ratio for institutions with undergraduate students. Only academic-year institutions report entering-class data; institutions with less-than-one-year programs do not have retention data. Retention covers students beginning in fall 2021 and persisting or completing in fall 2022.

Institutional revenues, expenditures, endowments, assets, liabilities, and financial-health measures for public institutions using GASB 34/35 accounting standards. The row grain is one public GASB institution, and the form includes detailed endowment data in addition to the common finance measures.

Institutional revenues, expenditures, endowments, assets, liabilities, and financial-health measures for private not-for-profit institutions and public institutions using FASB accounting standards. The row grain is one institution using the FASB model; unlike the for-profit FASB form, this form includes endowment data.

Institutional revenues, expenditures, assets, liabilities, and financial-health measures for private for-profit institutions using FASB accounting standards. The row grain is one private for-profit FASB institution; this form does not include endowment data.

Graduation outcomes at 100%, 150%, and 200% of normal time for 2014 cohorts at four-year institutions and 2018 cohorts at less-than-4-year institutions. The table distinguishes bachelor’s-seeking outcomes at four-year institutions from any degree/certificate completion at less-than-4-year institutions; records are organized by institution and cohort/outcome status, identified by UNITID and GRTYPE.

Graduation outcomes at 100% and 150% of normal time, including transfers, broken down by gender and race/ethnicity for four-year and two-year institution cohorts. Records are uniquely identified by UNITID and GRTYPE; four-year records distinguish bachelor’s-seeking from other degree/certificate-seeking students, while two-year records cover the 2019 full-time, first-time cohort and do not provide 100%-of-normal-time completion by gender and race/ethnicity.

Counts of students classified outside the IPEDS men/women categories in revised graduation-rate cohorts, with no completion or transfer outcomes. Records are organized by UNITID and the revised cohort/status identifier GRTYPE.

Graduation and transfer outcomes at 100% and 150% of normal time for the 2019 full-time, first-time degree/certificate-seeking undergraduate cohort at less-than-2-year institutions. Records are at the institution/cohort-status grain, identified by UNITID and GRTYPE, without the gender and race/ethnicity breakdowns in the main table.

Graduation outcomes at 150% of normal time for three financial-aid subcohorts: Pell Grant recipients; subsidized Stafford Loan recipients who did not receive Pell; and students receiving neither. Records are uniquely identified by UNITID and PSGRTYPE; four-year records cover 2016 bachelor’s-seeking and other degree/certificate-seeking cohorts, while two-year and less-than-2-year records cover 2019 full-time, first-time cohorts.

Fall staff counts broken down by full- or part-time status, medical school status, occupational category, faculty status, tenure status, and contract length for staff without tenure-track status. Each row is uniquely identified by UNITID and EAPCAT, which combines occupational category and faculty/tenure status.

Fall counts of full-time instructional staff at degree-granting institutions with 15 or more full-time employees and related administrative offices, broken down by faculty and tenure status, academic rank, race/ethnicity, and gender, with contract-length detail for staff not on tenure track or without a tenure system. Each row is uniquely identified by UNITID and SISCAT, combining faculty/tenure status and academic rank. Race/ethnicity and gender reporting was mandatory annually beginning in 2016; before then it was mandatory in odd-numbered years and optional in even-numbered years, so 2022 (even) has data under the annual-reporting rule.

Full-time permanent new-hire counts at degree-granting institutions with 15 or more full-time employees and related administrative offices, broken down by primary occupational category, race/ethnicity, gender, and, for instructional staff, faculty/tenure status and contract length. The new-hire period is November 1, 2021, through October 31, 2022; each row is uniquely identified by UNITID and SNHCAT, which combines primary occupation with instructional faculty/tenure status. Race/ethnicity and gender reporting was mandatory annually beginning in 2016; before then it was mandatory in odd-numbered years and optional in even-numbered years, so 2022 (even) has data under the annual-reporting rule.

Fall staff counts broken down by occupational category, race/ethnicity, gender, and full- or part-time status. Each row is uniquely identified by UNITID and STAFFCAT, which combines occupational category and full- or part-time status. Race/ethnicity and gender reporting was mandatory annually beginning in 2016; before then it was mandatory in odd-numbered years and optional in even-numbered years, so 2022 (even) has data under the annual-reporting rule.

Fall counts of full-time instructional staff at degree-granting institutions with 15 or more full-time employees and related administrative offices, broken down by academic rank, faculty and tenure status, and contract length for staff not on tenure track or without a tenure system. Each row is uniquely identified by UNITID and FACSTAT, the faculty/tenure-status classification.

Counts, salary outlays, average salaries, and equated 9-month salary measures for full-time, nonmedical instructional staff, broken down by academic rank (ARANK), gender, and months worked, including 9-, 10-, 11-, 12-month, and less-than-9-month categories. Each row is identified by UNITID and ARANK; salary data are unavailable for staff working less than 9 months.
Counts and salary outlays for full-time, nonmedical, noninstructional staff, broken down by occupational category.

Custom comparison-group membership records for the 2023 IPEDS Data Feedback Report, identified by the submitting group context and comparison institution, with the comparison institution’s unitid, name, and state.

Survey-component response-status records, identified by institution and survey component, showing response, imputation, applicability, parent/child or multi-campus reporting, and revised-data status in final or revised releases.

Institution directory records, one row per institution identified by IPEDS unitid, containing names and locations, institutional contact and web-link fields, active and Title IV participation status, and derived institutional classifications such as control, level, highest offering, highest degree, and Carnegie classification.

Institution-level records identified by unitid covering educational offerings and award levels, control and affiliations, admissions policy, distance education, library services, athletic associations, special learning opportunities, noncredit education, and Promise-program participation. The less-than-1-year certificate level is split into less-than-12-weeks and at-least-12-weeks-but-less-than-1-year categories from 2020-21 onward; 2022-23 also includes the added noncredit, special-learning-opportunity, and Promise-program variables.

Full-academic-year student-charge records for institutions with primarily academic, credit-hour programs using semester, quarter, trimester, 4-1-4, or other academic calendars. The table contains undergraduate and graduate tuition and required fees, part-time per-credit-hour charges, typical professional-practice doctoral charges, and published full-time first-time undergraduate attendance costs including tuition and fees, books and supplies, room and board, and other expenses.

Branch-campus location records, with one row per branch location listed by a reporting main campus in College Navigator, containing the location’s name and address, institutional links and classifications, award levels offered, and attendance-cost fields where the branch enrolls full-time first-time undergraduates. This is an optional, noncomprehensive list of reported College Navigator locations rather than a complete Title IV branch-campus inventory.

Program-level student-charge records for institutions using clock hours or primarily occupational credit-hour programs, identified by institution and program. It contains the number of programs, attendance costs for entering students in the largest program, and tuition and fees plus books and supplies for up to five additional programs.
Institution-level mission-statement records identified by unitid, containing either the institution’s mission statement or the web address where it is provided.

Award and enrollment outcomes for degree- and certificate-seeking undergraduates who entered degree-granting institutions from July 1, 2013, through June 30, 2014, measured at four, six, and eight years; the eight-year status is as of August 31, 2022. The population is divided into four entering-status/enrollment-intensity cohorts—first-time full-time, first-time part-time, non-first-time full-time, and non-first-time part-time—and each is split into Pell recipients and non-Pell recipients, with every student assigned to one subcohort. Each record is uniquely identified by IPEDS ID (UNITID) and cohort (OMCHRT) and contains the adjusted cohort size, numbers and percentages completing, and numbers and percentages still enrolled.

Student financial aid counts and total and average dollars by aid source and type for full-time, first-time degree/certificate-seeking undergraduates and for all undergraduates. The reporting grain is institution × undergraduate population/status × aid type: beginning in 2021–22, all undergraduates are separated into degree/certificate-seeking and non-degree/non-certificate-seeking groups; Pell grants and federal loans are reported for degree/certificate-seeking undergraduates, while total grants or scholarships are reported for both statuses.

Average net price and its supporting financial-aid amounts for two populations of full-time, first-time degree/certificate-seeking undergraduates: those receiving grant or scholarship aid and those receiving Title IV federal aid. For public institutions, both populations are limited to students paying the in-district or in-state tuition rate; the reporting grain is institution × net-price population.

Counts of students receiving military, servicemember, or veterans’ assistance and the total dollars received through the institution, separated by benefit type—Post-9/11 GI Bill Benefits and the Department of Defense Tuition Assistance Program—and by undergraduate versus graduate status. The reporting grain is institution × student level × benefit type.
